settings.help: Public webinars only — mentor 1:1 sessions never use the CBM Zoom account.
settings.label: Zoom webinar provisioning

settings.help: Pushes the CRM's opted-in contacts to the mailing service's list each night and pulls unsubscribes back each hour. Needs the mailing service credentials AND a connected account (Readiness → Mailing list sync).
settings.label: Mailing list sync

settings.help: The only time-driven follow-up. Needs the EventReminder template in the CRM; every send refuses by name until it exists.
settings.label: Event reminder emails

settings.help: Serves the Website group's values, images and key pages to the chapter website at /api/website/…. Public and unauthenticated by design; off, those addresses answer 404. Read per request.
settings.label: Chapter website connection

settings.help: Only the Chapter website addresses (and this app) may show the public forms in a frame, the forms report their height to that website, and a form opened with ?embed=1 takes the Website colours and drops its own heading and footer. Before switching on, put EVERY website that frames a form today into Chapter website addresses, or its forms go blank.
settings.label: Forms in website frames

settings.help: The public form at /newsletter/: a subscriber becomes a Contact with marketing consent, which the mailing-list sync passes to the mailing service. Off, the form answers 404.
settings.label: Newsletter signup form

settings.help: The free business evaluation a mentor offers a new client: the public survey pages at /evaluation/… and, in later phases, the Evaluations tab. Off, those addresses answer 404 and no existing page changes. Read per request. Needs the CBusinessEvaluation entity in the CRM (business-evaluation-crm-handoff.md).
settings.label: Business Evaluation

settings.help: Days a Business Evaluation link stays open after it is made. A link made earlier keeps the expiry it was given.
settings.label: Evaluation link lifetime

settings.help: Seconds between the worker's passes that send a submitted survey the CRM refused at the time. The answers are kept until it succeeds. 0 stops the pass.
settings.label: Evaluation retry interval

settings.help: The Marketing Management tile, the Prospects grid and import, the postcard kind and the campaign links at /c/. Read per request: no restart. Needs the CProspect, COutreachCampaign and COutreachTouch entities in the CRM (coutreach-entities-crm-handoff.md).
settings.label: Marketing Management

settings.help: The public page a postcard's QR code opens (/p/{token}). Off, the page answers 404; a card already mailed waits for it.
settings.label: Postcard landing page

settings.help: How often the worker looks for a signed-off postcard campaign to run. 0 disables the run.
settings.label: Campaign run poll

settings.help: The Call campaign kind and the Calls screen (prospect marketing Phase 3). Callers are the members of the teams named on each campaign (ruling 36). Read per request: no restart.
settings.label: Campaign calls

settings.help: An Unverified or Qualified prospect record with no touch for this many days leaves by the Stale side exit. 0 makes every untouched record stale — for a live check only.
settings.label: Prospect stale after

settings.help: The email campaign kind: each campaign's opted-in people pushed as its own named list at the mailing service, where staff design and send the notice. Needs the mailing connection (Mailing list sync's client ID and secret).
settings.label: Campaign emails

settings.help: Named lists a campaign sends to (build plan § 7c): the Lists page in Marketing Management and the List picker on a campaign. Off, every campaign selects by its kind's own rule, as before. Read per request: no restart.
settings.label: Campaign lists

settings.help: A list may keep a copy in Constant Contact, kept current by the mailing pass, and an email campaign sends to its list's copy: sign-off syncs it, staff send the notice at the mailing service, then pick that email in the campaign. Every push writes each person's lead code to the custom field cbm_lead_code. Needs Campaign lists and the mailing connection. Off, lists and email campaigns work as before.
settings.label: Campaign list copies

settings.help: Every campaign sends to a list: the per-kind rule boxes go, five ready-made lists stand in for them, and the campaign page shows its stage strip and the Audience and content tab. A campaign already built by a rule box is given its kind's ready-made list. Needs Campaign lists. Read per request: no restart. Off, campaigns work as before.
settings.label: Campaigns send to lists only

settings.help: Each email campaign's Constant Contact report is read for 30 days after its email is picked: one touch per recipient — delivered or bounced, opens and clicks — and the campaign completes when the 30 days end. Also the Recipients tab's Read the report now. Needs Campaign lists, Campaign list copies and the mailing connection. Off, nothing is read.
settings.label: Campaign send report

settings.help: Seconds between the worker's reads of the send reports (default a day). 0 stops the reads.
settings.label: Campaign send report interval

settings.help: The Lists tab redesigned: it opens on a searchable list of every list, with a Preview panel; Edit and View are screens of their own, and View opens the members in a separate browser tab. Needs Campaign lists. Read per request: no restart. Off, the Lists tab is the one built before.
settings.label: Campaign list screens

settings.help: A Promote this event button on an event in Event Administration makes one draft campaign per ticked channel, each linked to the event, with a link to its registration page and the chosen list; the event gains a Campaigns tab counting who each campaign reached, registered and attended. Needs Marketing Management and Campaign lists. Read per request: no restart. Off, Event Administration shows neither.
settings.label: Promote this event

settings.help: The Calls tab with a count line, the brief at the top, attempts and the last attempt per row, and a side panel holding what we know, the person's own link and the four outcomes; Call again takes a time, and recording moves to the next row. Read per request: no restart. Off, the Calls tab works as before.
settings.label: Calls tab side panel

settings.help: Seconds between the worker's passes that re-run every active dynamic list and count every active list's members and reach (default a day). 0 stops the pass; Refresh on a list still counts that list.
settings.label: Campaign list count interval

settings.help: The fields a list step may filter on, per record type (ruling 63), written as 'lead: leadStatus, leadSource; contact: cContactType, cFunnelStage'. Use the CRM's field names; a dotted name follows links (client: engagementClient.industrySector). Record types: lead, contact, client, partner, funder. Empty uses the defaults. Each field is checked against the CRM when saved; a field the CRM lacks is refused.
settings.label: Campaign list fields

settings.help: The text-message campaign kind (rulings 38, 39). The application sends the texts through the texting service below — with 'Texting service' at dryrun nothing is texted. Needs COutreachCampaign.smsMessage in the CRM.
settings.label: Campaign texts

settings.help: The free pass: the worker scores every open lead 0 to 100 for fit (prds/lead-enrichment/). Needs the nine fit fields on CProspect (lead-fit-score-crm-handoff.md). Writes nothing but the score fields, and a verified website into an empty website field.
settings.label: Lead fit scores

settings.help: Lets the free pass fetch web addresses guessed from a lead's name and keep one only when the page shows the name and the address or an associate (ruling E12). Off, no outside request is made.
settings.label: Lead web checks

settings.help: How often the worker scores a batch of leads. 0 stops the sweep; /setup → Operations → Lead fit scores still runs it by hand.
settings.label: Lead fit sweep

settings.help: Leads scored per pass, at most 200 (the CRM's page limit).
settings.label: Lead fit batch

settings.help: The chapter's counties as State:County pairs separated by |, for example OH:Cuyahoga|OH:Lake. A lead confirmed outside them scores 0 and is flagged Out of area. Empty: the location is not checked. Changing it rescores every lead.
settings.label: Service area counties

settings.help: Three numbers: operating business, segment, findability. 1,1,1 weighs them equally. Changing it rescores every lead.
settings.label: Fit score weights

settings.help: The address of the chapter's segment list, a JSON file with "favoured" and "excluded" lists of industries or words. Empty: every lead scores 50 for segment.
settings.label: Segment list address

settings.help: The address of a chapter's own version of the name-reading rules (enrichment/data/name_terms.json). Empty: the shipped rules.
settings.label: Name rules address

settings.help: Lets staff start an AI research run on a lead, a set of leads or a client's company (prds/lead-enrichment/, ruling E18). Needs the Anthropic API key and the CEnrichmentFinding entity (enrichment-finding-crm-handoff.md). Read per request.
settings.label: AI research

settings.help: The Claude model the research runs on. claude-opus-5-5 by default.
settings.label: AI research model

settings.help: What paid enrichment may spend in a calendar month (rulings E8, E9). A run that would pass it is refused, with the amounts named.
settings.label: Enrichment monthly budget

settings.help: Web searches the model may make for one business ($0.01 each).
settings.label: AI research searches per business

settings.help: A business whose research passes this cost is stopped and marked failed.
settings.label: AI research cap per business

settings.help: The most records one run may take.
settings.label: AI research records per run

settings.help: When the model declines a request, re-run it on the next model automatically. Off: a declined business is marked failed.
settings.label: AI research fallback

settings.help: How often the worker takes the next records from the queue. 0 stops it.
settings.label: AI research queue poll

settings.help: The level inside Qualified — Identified, Contactable, Referred — placed by the system and settable by hand, never moved backwards; the Leads tab's counts, Level and Reach columns, Assigned to, and the lead's own page. Needs the redesign's lead fields on the CRM (marketing-redesign-crm-handoff.md); without them the Leads tab stays as before. Read per request: no restart.
settings.label: Lead qualification ladder

settings.help: How often the worker re-places the level of leads edited since its last pass (catches edits made in the CRM's own screens). 0 stops the sweep; /setup → Operations → Lead levels still runs it by hand.
settings.label: Lead level sweep

settings.help: The import tool on the Imports tab: saved templates for recurring spreadsheets, Excel as well as CSV, recognition of the matching template with the differences shown, the four column fixes, a preview the delivery worker computes while the page polls, repeat rows filling a lead's empty fields, the level per row, and Undo this import. Off, the Imports tab and the CSV import behave exactly as before. Read per request: no restart.
settings.label: Import templates

settings.help: On a lead's page: Email through the full composer from the assignee's own chapter mailbox (the mentor profile's address, else the user's own on the mail domain), Log a call with Interested / Not interested / No reply yet, a Conversations block, and the email sync attaching a reply from an assigned lead's address to the lead and marking it Replied. Needs the lead's Assigned to and Replied fields and the conversation link on the CRM (marketing-redesign-crm-handoff.md), the Gmail integration, and the chapter postal address under Presentation. Read per request: no restart.
settings.label: Personal outreach to leads

settings.help: How often the delivery worker looks for an import preview waiting to be computed. 0 stops it — then no import can be previewed, and the page says so after two minutes.
settings.label: Import plan poll

settings.help: How often the worker runs the Stale sweep (default nightly). 0 disables it; /setup → Operations still runs it by hand.
settings.label: Prospect stale sweep

settings.help: The whole Communications pipeline. Needs the Google service account.
settings.label: Gmail conversation sync

settings.help: Saving a Scheduled session reconciles an event on the manager's calendar.
settings.label: Google Calendar events

settings.help: Do NOT switch on before the meetings.space.created DWD scope exists — every Scheduled save would show mentors a transcription failure.
settings.label: Meet transcripts

settings.help: Worker-only: Fathom auto-joins from the mentor's own calendar.
settings.label: Fathom transcripts

settings.help: The Documents tab. Needs a database and the shared drive.
settings.label: Google Drive documents

settings.help: The '+ Add partner' / '+ Add funder' button on those grids. Creates the company, primary contact and profile as the signed-in user.
settings.label: Add partners & funders in-app

settings.help: The nightly clean-up, a Mentor Administration save, Update Mentor Status and provisioning copy a mentor's login only when the login data agrees (one profile, its CBM email matching). Otherwise they leave it and log a fault.
settings.label: Stop login repairs on disagreement

settings.help: A login on several mentor profiles opens only the one Active profile whose CBM email matches the login. Otherwise Client Management and My Mentor Profile show no records and say why.
settings.label: Strict mentor profile choice

settings.help: In Mentor Administration the CBM email can't be edited once the mentor has a login; it shows the login's user name. Before then a typed address must be on the chapter's mail domain and not already a login or another mentor's address.
settings.label: Lock the mentor CBM email

settings.help: Once a day the worker checks every mentor profile, login and mentor Contact for the six login faults and records what it finds. Report only: a log line and scripts/integrity_report.py. Sends no email.
settings.label: Daily login integrity check

settings.help: The integrity digest: one email a day listing every open login fault, new ones marked. Also the fault list and the badge in Mentor Administration. Turn on only after reading this instance's first report.
settings.label: Tell staff about login faults

settings.help: A History tab on a mentor profile (Mentor Administration), an engagement (Client Administration), a partner or funder (Partner and Funder Management) and an event (Event Administration). It lists the applications' recorded actions and the CRM's own record changes, newest first, with old and new values. Never shown in Client Management.
settings.label: History tab on records

settings.help: A page listing every change by one person, or in a date range, across every record, with a CSV export. For the System Management Team; administrators always see it.
settings.label: Activity page

settings.help: Once a day the web component reads the CRM's Action History and sign-in log as the administrator and records who created, changed or deleted records in the CRM's own screens, and any screen sign-in by a shared account. Listed in the login fault list and the integrity digest.
settings.label: Report work in the CRM's own screens

settings.help: When a login with no mentor profile opens Client Management or My Mentor Profile, record it and (with the integrity digest on) email at once, at most once per login per day.
settings.label: Alert when a login has no mentor profile

settings.help: The rail of upcoming events beside the portal's tiles, and the member page each one opens. Members see Internal events (to their teams, if limited) and this chapter's Public webinars. Needs Events & Webinars on.
settings.label: Events on the portal home page

settings.help: How many days ahead the rail lists in full; events beyond fold behind one line. 0 folds everything.
settings.label: Portal calendar window

settings.help: The Presenters group in the event editor and the presenter cards on the public and portal event pages. Stays hidden until the CRM has CEventPresenter, so it is safe to switch on early.
settings.label: Presenters on events

settings.help: CBM's own confirmation to each event registrant, from the EspoCRM templates EventConfirmation, EventWaitlisted and EventSeatOffered, as the shared mailbox. Zoom's own confirmations are off, so this is the registrant's only email. Needs Gmail sync and the shared mailbox.
settings.label: Registration confirmation emails

settings.help: The Grants tab in Funder Management — awards, deliverables and (later) funder reporting. Stays hidden until the CRM has CGrant and CGrantDeliverable, so it is safe to switch on early.
settings.label: Grants on funder records

settings.help: Optional. Requires ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
settings.label: AI conversation summaries

settings.help: Needs Gmail sync, the shared mailbox and the database.
settings.label: Daily email digest

settings.help: Creates an EspoCRM User on approval, via the admin service account.
settings.label: Provision mentor logins

settings.help: Blocks provisioning when a mailbox is confirmed missing. Fails open.
settings.label: Verify CBM mailbox exists

settings.help: Needs the read-WRITE Directory scope.
settings.label: Create missing mailboxes

settings.help: Capture returns immediately and the worker delivers with retries. Off = synchronous. Needs a database.
settings.label: Asynchronous delivery

settings.help: Clears every mailbox cursor on worker start so the next pass re-runs the backfill. Set it, let ONE pass complete, then turn it off — left on, every restart re-reads all mailboxes. A good candidate for a temporary override.
settings.label: Gmail one-shot resync

settings.help: 'dryrun' mails nothing and produces the preview pieces. 'lob' is the real adapter and needs the key below.
settings.label: Mail vendor

settings.help: The vendor's API key. With 'Mail vendor test mode' on, a test key is the right one: the whole pipeline runs and nothing is printed.
settings.label: Mail vendor API key

settings.help: Signs the delivery and return events the vendor posts to /api/campaigns/postal/events. Unset, that route is not mounted.
settings.label: Mail vendor webhook secret

settings.help: On (the default), even a real key mails nothing. Switch it off for ONE real run and back on afterwards (build plan § 7 Phase 1).
settings.label: Mail vendor test mode

settings.help: The per-piece price from the vendor's price sheet; the sign-off shows pieces × this. 0 (the dry run's price) until the vendor is chosen.
settings.label: Postcard unit cost

settings.help: The three-letter code the estimated cost is written in (the CRM's currency field needs it on every write).
settings.label: Postcard cost currency

settings.help: 'dryrun' texts nothing. 'twilio' sends for real and needs the account, the sender number and the carrier registration (A2P 10DLC) first.
settings.label: Texting service

settings.help: Sends the texts (worker) and verifies the replies and delivery reports the service posts back (web).
settings.label: Texting auth token

settings.help: The number texts come from, in +1… form.
settings.label: Texting sender number

settings.help: Hours a text may go out, chapter time, as start-end (9-20 = 9:00 to 19:59).
settings.label: Texting hours

settings.help: The time zone the texting hours are read in.
settings.label: Texting time zone

settings.help: 'service' is the operational mode — nobody is a shared-drive member.
settings.label: Drive identity

settings.help: Entity=Label pairs, e.g. CEngagement=Clients.
settings.label: Drive folder labels

settings.help: 0 disables the nightly job.
settings.label: Drive grant reconciliation

settings.help: Must be a real licensed mailbox — a group or alias 403s.
settings.label: Delegated Workspace admin

settings.help: Google Group a mentor's new mailbox joins when their account is created. Blank skips the group step. Needs the Directory group scope.
settings.label: All Members group

settings.help: Shared by the Meet and Fathom sources.
settings.label: Transcript retrieval

settings.help: Keep inside Google's 30-day transcript retention.
settings.label: Transcript give-up window

settings.help: The recorded-webinar playlists to import from, comma separated. CBM keeps five topic playlists rather than one library. A video in two of them is imported once. Read only by the import script.
settings.label: YouTube playlists

settings.help: The key behind Gmail, Calendar, Drive and Directory. Checked for shape before it is stored; whether domain-wide delegation has been granted cannot be seen from here.
settings.label: Google service account

settings.help: AI conversation summaries only.
settings.label: Anthropic API key

settings.help: Public webinars only. Mentor sessions never use the CBM Zoom account.
settings.label: Zoom client secret

settings.help: The developer application's API key (Constant Contact). One application per deployment, created by the account's own user — it is private to them.
settings.label: Mailing service client ID

settings.help: Shown once by the vendor when generated. Its check is the Connect step on the Readiness tab — nothing can probe it without a user authorising.
settings.label: Mailing service client secret

settings.help: The list the push maintains; found by name, created when absent.
settings.label: Mailing list name

settings.help: 0 disables the push and leaves the pull.
settings.label: Mailing push interval

settings.help: 0 disables the pull of unsubscribes.
settings.label: Mailing pull interval

settings.help: Override only for a vendor change.
settings.label: Mailing service API base URL

settings.help: The recorded-webinar library.
settings.label: YouTube API key

settings.help: Submission Admin sends and reads as this. Must be a REAL mailbox, not a group. Only ONE environment may poll it — setting it on both double-captures.
settings.label: Shared mailbox

settings.help: The domain this system's invented training addresses sit on, such as sandbox.mentorsassociation.org. Nothing is ever sent to, shared with, added to a group as, or put on a mailing list as an address on it. Blank on a system with no training data.
settings.label: Sandbox address domain

settings.help: 0 turns inbound capture off.
settings.label: Inbound poll

settings.help: Must be a real licensed mailbox; falls back to the shared mailbox.
settings.label: Alert sender

settings.help: How long the sync may reuse its map of who handles which records before rebuilding it from the CRM. Between rebuilds each pass only asks the CRM whether anything changed. 0 rebuilds every pass.
settings.label: Mailbox scope rebuild

settings.help: Who receives the integrity digest and the no-profile sign-in alert. Empty uses the alert recipients.
settings.label: Login fault recipients

settings.help: Local hour of the daily login integrity check; the digest follows it, and the report on the CRM's own screens runs an hour before. On the training sandbox a time between 04:00 and 06:00 UTC moves to 06:00 UTC.
settings.label: Integrity check hour

settings.help: Logins whose sign-in to the CRM's own screens is reported. Empty means admin, and admin@ and mentoradmin@ the mentor email domain.
settings.label: Shared CRM accounts

settings.help: Never reported for editing in the CRM's own screens. The provisioning and key-based accounts are left out automatically.
settings.label: Logins not reported for CRM edits

settings.help: Addresses known to be this application, so its traffic is never counted as use of the CRM's own screens. Usually found automatically; empty is normal.
settings.label: This application's network addresses

settings.help: Mail between these domains links to Contacts, never records.
settings.label: Internal domains

settings.help: Mentor logins and mailboxes are minted as firstname.lastname@ this domain.
settings.label: Mentor email domain

settings.help: MIME types (text/calendar) or filenames/extensions (.ics, winmail.dat) that inbound mail never files to a record's Documents tab. The bytes stay in the message — View original still shows them.
settings.label: Never file these attachments

settings.help: 0 disables the hold entirely.
settings.label: Near-duplicate hold

settings.help: How long a claimed row stays leased before reclaim.
settings.label: Delivery lease

settings.help: 0 disables.
settings.label: Schema-drift check

settings.help: Runs on WEB — a dead worker can't alert on itself.
settings.label: Worker liveness watch

settings.help: 0 disables the timer.
settings.label: Receipt reconciliation

settings.help: 0 disables.
settings.label: Assignment-stamp reconciliation

settings.help: How often finished online events are checked for a Zoom participant report.
settings.label: Attendance pull

settings.help: How long after an event ends before its report is first asked for — an empty report means 'not published yet', never 'nobody came'.
settings.label: Attendance grace

settings.help: When to stop asking. Past this an event's attendance stays as it is.
settings.label: Attendance give-up

settings.help: How often the worker looks for reminders that are due.
settings.label: Reminder sweep

settings.help: How far ahead of an event a reminder goes out. Never sent after an event has started, so a worker that was down through the window stays quiet rather than sending late.
settings.label: Reminder lead time

settings.help: How often each process re-reads the overrides on this page. Web and worker refresh independently; /healthz reports each one's version.
settings.label: Settings refresh

settings.help: How long a session's cached team membership stays trusted.
settings.label: Membership re-read

settings.help: How long field definitions, layouts, labels and enum options are remembered before the CRM is asked again. A field built in the CRM shows within this window. 0 reads the CRM on every request.
settings.label: CRM metadata cache

settings.help: The web log carries one 'timing' line per API request: total time, CRM calls and their time. 0 logs every API request; a higher value logs only the requests slower than it.
settings.label: Timing log threshold

settings.help: A regular user's token cannot read its own roles — prefer teams.
settings.label: Client Administration (roles)

settings.help: The team whose members see the activity page (and later System Management functions). Copy the team's name exactly; administrators always pass.
settings.label: System Management

settings.help: Stamped on new CPartnerProfiles. Empty disables the stamp.
settings.label: Partner team stamp

settings.help: This chapter's short label in the chapter list of the CRM standard — cleveland, boston. Every public event's reach includes it. It must be one of the options of the event Chapters field, or the reach is left alone.
settings.label: Chapter short label

settings.help: Linked from the consent checkbox on the public forms.
settings.label: Client code of conduct URL

settings.help: The volunteer form's Code of Conduct link — a different document.
settings.label: Mentor code of ethics URL

settings.help: Overrides the auto-derived Production/Test/Dev wording in the footer.
settings.label: Environment label

settings.help: Used for deep links in alert emails and the digest.
settings.label: This app's public URL

settings.help: Empty means this app's own /webinars/, derived from the public URL above — which is almost always what you want.
settings.label: Public event page base

settings.help: The line under the heading on /webinars/. Empty removes it.
settings.label: Programme page tagline

settings.help: The short third line in the hero. Empty removes it.
settings.label: Programme page pillars

settings.help: A publicly-hosted image for events with no picture of their own. Last fallback only — an event's own graphic wins, and a recording's video thumbnail wins over this. Mainly fixes the empty social-share card an image-less event otherwise has. Empty means no image.
settings.label: Default event graphic

settings.help: The gold strapline under the hero. Empty removes it.
settings.label: Programme page band

settings.help: Who the "Interested in Presenting or Hosting?" panel writes to. Empty falls back to the shared mailbox; with both empty the panel carries no address rather than a dead link.
settings.label: Programme contact address

settings.help: The name every page carries — title, footer and the public forms' prose. Substituted server-side as it is served, so a change here takes effect on the next page load with no redeploy.
settings.label: Organisation name

settings.help: The short form of the name, CBM for Cleveland. Every page, message and email that used to say CBM says this instead — "ask CBM staff", the "CBM contacts" table, the daily digest subject. Substituted as pages are served, so a change takes effect on the next page load.
settings.label: Chapter acronym

settings.help: The chapter's mailing address, one or more lines. Every personal email a lead receives ends with the sentence offering a way to say no AND this address (the server appends both when the message lacks them). Empty, personal email is refused and the refusal names this setting.
settings.label: Chapter postal address

settings.help: A publicly-hosted https image (typically on the org's own website). Powers the email-signature editor's Insert-logo button — signature images must be reachable without a login. The website uses the logo uploaded under Website images below, and this address only when none is uploaded.
settings.label: Organisation logo URL

settings.help: URL of a stylesheet redefining --cbm-* custom properties on :root. Loaded after the base tokens; custom properties only, never selectors.
settings.label: Chapter design-token override

settings.help: The public site. Every /webinars/ page links back to it, and it is the base the menu below resolves its paths against.
settings.label: Organisation website

settings.help: Reproduced across the top of the public pages so a visitor is not stranded. "Label|path" pairs, comma separated; a leading / is resolved against the website above. Empty renders no menu.
settings.label: Website menu

settings.help: The chapter website's own addresses, such as https://example.org — scheme and host only, comma separated. Only these may fetch the website's content from a visitor's browser (the mentor search). Separate from Allowed origins, which covers every address of this app.
settings.label: Chapter website addresses

settings.help: The page background. A colour written #RRGGBB.
settings.label: Colour — background

settings.help: Body text and headings. A colour written #RRGGBB.
settings.label: Colour — text

settings.help: Links, headings and the main buttons. A colour written #RRGGBB.
settings.label: Colour — main brand

settings.help: A pale version of the main brand colour, for soft panels. #RRGGBB.
settings.label: Colour — light brand tint

settings.help: The second brand colour: call-to-action buttons and key accents. #RRGGBB.
settings.label: Colour — highlight

settings.help: Secondary text such as captions and dates. #RRGGBB.
settings.label: Colour — muted text

settings.help: Bands and cards that sit on the page background. #RRGGBB.
settings.label: Colour — light section background

settings.help: Lines and borders. #RRGGBB.
settings.label: Colour — borders

settings.help: A font list as a stylesheet writes it, such as Georgia, serif. Letters, digits, spaces, commas, quotes and hyphens only.
settings.label: Font — headings

settings.help: As for the heading font.
settings.label: Font — body text

settings.help: The one public contact address the website shows, in its footer and on its Contact page.
settings.label: Chapter contact email

settings.help: Shown in the website footer beside the 501(c)(3) statement. Written 12-3456789.
settings.label: Employer identification number

settings.help: The hosted payment page the website's Donate button opens, such as a Stripe Payment Link. An https address.
settings.label: Donation payment page

settings.help: "Label|https://…" pairs, comma separated, such as LinkedIn|https://www.linkedin.com/company/example.
settings.label: Social media addresses

settings.help: How long the key pages keep what they read from the CRM. A change in the CRM reaches the website within this time plus the website's own few minutes. The mentor search uses the kept list, never the CRM.
settings.label: Key page refresh

settings.help: Shows the mentor directory and profiles on the website, with their menu entry. A mentor appears when Active and Public profile is ticked.
settings.label: Key page — Find a Mentor

settings.help: The upcoming published events, by the same rule as the public programme page.
settings.label: Key page — Workshops and Events

settings.help: The published recorded webinars.
settings.label: Key page — Recordings

settings.help: Refused: partners on the website is a feature request owed to the Association's committee.
settings.label: Key page — Our Partners

settings.help: Refused: sponsors on the website is a feature request owed to the Association's committee.
settings.label: Key page — Our Sponsors

settings.help: Refused: client stories need recorded consent, a feature request owed to the Association's committee.
settings.label: Key page — Client Stories

settings.help: Mounts the /analytics routes and its portal tile. The routes do not exist until the process restarts, so switching this on mid-run would otherwise produce a tile leading nowhere.
settings.label: Analytics

settings.help: Mounts the /events routes and its portal tile.
settings.label: Events & Webinars

settings.help: The unauthenticated read API the website's programme reads. Publishing is still gated per event.
settings.label: Public events API

settings.help: The whole staff stack — portal, Client Administration and the rest. Turning this off leaves only the public intake forms.
settings.label: Staff applications

settings.help: Applied once by logging setup as the process starts.
settings.label: Log level

settings.help: Built into the middleware at startup. Submissions allowed per window from one address.
settings.label: Intake rate limit

settings.help: The window the limit above is counted over.
settings.label: Intake rate window

settings.help: Built into the middleware at startup. Chiefly the volunteer form's optional resume.
settings.label: Maximum submission size

settings.help: How often to re-read the CRM's configuration version for the status page. 0 switches it off. The background task is created once at startup, so starting or stopping it needs a restart. /healthz always serves the cached answer and never waits on the CRM.
settings.label: CRM configuration check

settings.help: Which EspoCRM this deployment reads and writes. Checked before it is saved: the address must answer AND hold this application's entities, so pointing at a stranger's EspoCRM is refused rather than accepted.
settings.label: CRM address

settings.help: The org-wide key. Tried against the CRM before it is stored; a key the CRM rejects is refused. Never shown back once set.
settings.label: CRM API key

settings.help: On, nothing is ever written to the CRM and submissions are logged only. This is how the dev deployment runs.
settings.label: Dry run (no CRM writes)

settings.help: The admin service account used for the few operations EspoCRM reserves for admins — creating mentor logins, team membership.
settings.label: Provisioning admin username

settings.help: Never shown back once set.
settings.label: Provisioning admin password

settings.help: Signs every session cookie. Changing it signs EVERYONE out, including you — so confirm you can still sign in, or it reverts itself.
settings.label: Session signing secret

settings.help: On is correct for any real deployment. On over plain http, no one can sign in at all — hence the countdown.
settings.label: HTTPS-only session cookie

settings.help: Only matters if a separate frontend origin is ever introduced; the wizard posts to its own origin.
settings.label: Allowed origins

settings.help: Switching this off hides the page you are reading. It reverts itself unless confirmed, because otherwise recovery would need a redeploy.
settings.label: This Settings page

settings.help: The break-glass. Off, every stored setting stops applying and the deployment's own values take over — including the one that switched this off, so it could never switch itself back on. Reverts unless confirmed.
settings.label: Settings overrides

settings.help: The other environment, for the comparison on the Environment diff tab.
settings.label: Peer deployment URL

settings.help: Authorises that comparison. No secret value ever crosses the wire.
settings.label: Peer deployment token

settings.help: When the nightly wipe runs, in the timezone below. Meaningless unless the wipe itself is switched on.
settings.label: Sandbox wipe hour

settings.help: The timezone the hour above is read in.
settings.label: Sandbox wipe timezone

settings.help: Worker-side. Empties this deployment's own submission queue and document index every night. Correct on the training sandbox, ruinous anywhere else — which is why it is checked before it is stored.
settings.label: Nightly sandbox wipe

settings.help: Cannot be changed here, and this is a logical impossibility rather than caution: the stored settings live INSIDE this database, so a setting that moved the app elsewhere would be left behind in the database being abandoned, and the app would read its configuration from the new one and move straight back. Change it in the deployment configuration.
settings.label: Database

settings.help: Protects the secrets stored on this page and the Google configuration. Rotating it makes every one of them permanently unreadable — data loss, which no verification can undo. Rotation needs a re-encryption migration, not a text box.
settings.label: Encryption key

settings.help: Which release this container was built from — stamped into the image at build time and supplied by the deployment's own configuration. Read-only on purpose: a stored value would survive a restart and make this deployment misreport which build it is running. Empty means an untagged build.
settings.label: Release tag
